mariowOS Applications | Guidelines

1. Store and system guidelines

 1.1 Kernel Injection/Bridge layer
  Applications are composed by tree layers. UI -> Framework -> Bridge, which all run on the top part of mariowOS, aside bridge. Bridge connects the framework of your app to the kernel which only
  system and certified applications can access and use. The only reason to bridge through the kernel is for authentication, emulation or for developing DE's. If used for bad actions, your app will be
  straight up refused and you'll get banned. Kernel injection is forbidden, no apps can inject through the desktop if not for system-wide utilities (calendar, music or sideloading apps). 

1.2 Desktop Bar
  The desktop app will always be drawn by the desktop, only system apps. You can use a option bar like the notes app has for the options. If your app uses tabs, and complies with the guidelines, it
  can be whitelisted.

1.3 mariowOS Account
  Apps can access your mariowOS account information, but ONLY your profile picture, username and can prompt you to use your password for accessing features (1.1)

1.4 CLI apps
  You can build CLI applications that doesn't require direct access to the kernel (1.1). If, you need to build a super package you must comply with 1.1 and 1.3, and bridge cannot be accessed if not
  authorized by the user. You must prompt the user to input the password before authorizing any operation. Guardrails are here too. Your app HAS to be authorized and built in the terminal before
  anyone can use. 

1.5 

2. Design guidelines

2.1 Transparency
 mariowOS features transparency and blur everywhere, to improve readability we recommend to use these values:
  
 :root {
    --m3-dropdown-bg: rgba(24, 25, 28, 0.85);
    --m3-text-color: #e6e0e9;
    --m3-glass-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12);
    --m3-glass-shadow: 0 12px 40px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45);
    --m3-accent-active: #5c7cfa;
  }

 You can use different values if your application needs more blur or transparency. There are guardrails which is blur that is drawn by the desktop. You cannot make transparent applications.

2.2 Font
 Use Poppins for menus, but you can always use different fonts for your app. We recommend using Sans fonts which are accessible to everyone. Your font must come from Google Fonts and has
 to be implemented using their guidelines. Monospace fonts are accepted.
